statement: The function returns a result r, and r is the largest integer k with k >= 0 such that there exists an integer a for which every integer j with 0 <= j < k satisfies: the value a + j occurs at least once among nums[0], ..., nums[len(nums)-1]. For k = 0 the condition is vacuous; when len(nums) = 0 the largest such k is 0.
preconditions: len(nums) <= 100000 and for every index i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: For every slice nums satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r; it does not fail, panic, overflow, or access out of bounds.
preconditions: len(nums) <= 100000 and for every index i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, 0 <= r <= len(nums).
preconditions: len(nums) <= 100000 and for every index i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if len(nums) = 0 then r = 0.
preconditions: len(nums) <= 100000 and for every index i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if len(nums) > 0 then 1 <= r.
preconditions: len(nums) <= 100000 and for every index i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r and r > 0, there exists an integer a such that for every integer j with 0 <= j < r, the value a + j occurs at least once among nums[0], ..., nums[len(nums)-1].
preconditions: len(nums) <= 100000 and for every index i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, there is no integer a such that every integer j with 0 <= j <= r satisfies: the value a + j occurs at least once among nums[0], ..., nums[len(nums)-1].
preconditions: len(nums) <= 100000 and for every index i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: For all such slices xs and ys, if for every integer v, v occurs among xs[0], ..., xs[len(xs)-1] if and only if v occurs among ys[0], ..., ys[len(ys)-1], then whenever the calls longest_consecutive(xs) and longest_consecutive(ys) return results r_xs and r_ys respectively, r_xs = r_ys.
preconditions: For slices xs and ys, len(xs) <= 100000, len(ys) <= 100000, and every element of xs and every element of ys is between -1000000000 and 1000000000 inclusive.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if len(nums) > 0 and every integer v with min(nums) <= v <= max(nums) occurs at least once among nums[0], ..., nums[len(nums)-1], then r = max(nums) - min(nums) + 1, where min(nums) and max(nums) are the least and greatest entries of nums.
preconditions: len(nums) <= 100000 and for every index i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if len(nums) > 0 and no two distinct values occurring in nums differ by exactly 1, then r = 1.
preconditions: len(nums) <= 100000 and for every index i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if len(nums) = n > 0, then r = n if and only if the n entries nums[0], ..., nums[n-1] are pairwise distinct and max(nums) - min(nums) + 1 = n, where min(nums) and max(nums) are the least and greatest entries of nums.
preconditions: len(nums) <= 100000 and for every index i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r <= |{ nums[i] : 0 <= i < len(nums) }|, the number of distinct values occurring in nums.
preconditions: len(nums) <= 100000 and for every index i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if len(nums) > 0 then r <= max(nums) - min(nums) + 1, where min(nums) and max(nums) are the least and greatest entries of nums.
preconditions: len(nums) <= 100000 and for every index i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if there exist indices i and j with 0 <= i < len(nums), 0 <= j < len(nums), and nums[i] + 1 = nums[j], then r >= 2.
preconditions: len(nums) <= 100000 and for every index i with 0 <= i < len(nums), -1000000000 <= nums[i] <= 1000000000.
